title: Lighthouse upgrade executor for VPC: cohort rollouts, compatibility harbor, and transactional rollback
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a pragmatic, reproducible upgrade executor for Redwood Private deployments that performs cohort-based rollouts across VPC/on-prem fleets, enforces LTS compatibility gates, and provides transactional rollback on failure.

Scope: 
- Executor CLI + controller for scheduling upgrade cohorts (size, region, timing).
- Compatibility Harbor: a staging zone that validates binary, schema, and config compatibility using lightweight runtime emulation and canary traffic.
- Snapshot-and-apply semantics for stateful components (etcd/RocksDB snapshots, delta apply hooks).
- Policy-driven gates (success thresholds, latency/error budgets, custom probes) with automated rollback and quarantine paths.
- Observability: per-cohort dashboards, rollout telemetry, and a runbook for operators.

Design decisions: 
- Use immutable release bundles (image + manifest + compatibility metadata) to avoid partial diff upgrades.
- Prefer non-blocking schema transformers where possible; for unavoidable breaking migrations use transactionally staged applies with preflight dry-run.
- Keep controller stateless where possible; rely on durable snapshot storage in S3-compatible object storage for checkpoints.

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Rollouts can be created with cohort definitions and policy templates via CLI or API.
2) Compatibility Harbor runs automated checks within 15 minutes for small deployments and surfaces deterministic pass/fail reasons.
3) Successful rollback reverts to previous image and replays or discards delta state per policy without data loss in >95% of tests.
4) Integration tests (end-to-end) exist and run in CI protect branch on PRs.

Out-of-scope: full replacement of existing Private upgrade operator. This is an incremental tool to provide safer, repeatable upgrades while we converge operators later.
